items.title: A potential pathway to reversing liver fibrosis targets specialized immune cells
items.text: A new study by Western University researchers has identified a potential pathway to reversing liver fibrosis, a condition that can progress to life-threatening liver disease. Published in Science Advances, the findings demonstrate how specialized immune cells, known as mucosa-associated invariant T cells (MAIT cells), contribute to liver scarring—and how targeting them could help mitigate or reverse the damage.
